terms: Denaturation
Unfolding of protein structure by heat, acid or agitation; e.g. egg white setting on cooking.
Essential amino acids
Nine amino acids the body cannot synthesise and must obtain from food.
High biological value (HBV)
Protein containing all essential amino acids — typically animal sources plus soya and quinoa.
Low biological value (LBV)
Protein lacking one or more essential amino acids — most plant proteins.
Protein
Macronutrient made of amino acids; provides 4 kcal/g; needed for growth and repair.
Protein complementation
Combining LBV foods (e.g. beans and rice) to provide all essential amino acids.
Cost and income
A major factor in food choice, as the price of food relative to a household's budget limits which products people can afford to buy.
Dietary needs
Medical conditions, allergies and intolerances such as coeliac disease or nut allergy that require people to select or avoid particular foods.
Ethical and environmental concerns
Considerations such as animal welfare, Fairtrade, food miles and sustainability that influence which foods consumers decide to buy.
Lifestyle
Factors such as time, working hours and convenience that lead people to choose ready meals, takeaways or quick-cook foods to fit busy routines.
Religion and culture
Beliefs and traditions that shape food choice, such as halal and kosher rules or vegetarianism, determining which foods are permitted or avoided.
Sensory appeal
The influence of a food's appearance, aroma, taste, texture and sound on whether a consumer finds it desirable and chooses to eat it.
Core temperature
Cooking poultry to ≥75°C core for at least 30 seconds destroys most pathogens.
Critical control point (CCP)
A step where control is essential to prevent or eliminate a food safety hazard.
Cross-contamination
Transfer of harmful microorganisms between foods, surfaces or equipment.
Danger zone
5–63°C — temperature range where pathogenic bacteria multiply rapidly.
HACCP
Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points — systematic preventive approach to food safety.
Pathogenic bacteria
Salmonella, E. coli O157, Listeria, Campylobacter — cause food poisoning.

Adolescents
Calcium needs peak; UK RNI 1000 mg/day for 11–18-year-old girls.
Athletes
Increased carbohydrate for glycogen, protein for repair; hydration critical.
Children
Higher protein and calcium per kg body weight than adults; iron-rich foods support growth.
Infants
Exclusive breastfeeding recommended for first 6 months; weaning starts around 6 months.
Older adults
Lower energy needs but protein, vitamin D and B12 remain important; sarcopenia risk.
Pregnancy
Increased folate (400 µg/day pre-conception), iron, and avoidance of unpasteurised cheese and pâté.

Control variable
A condition, such as oven temperature or cooking time, kept constant during an experiment so it does not distort the comparison being made.
Evaluation
The stage of a research project where results are analysed against the original aim, conclusions are drawn and improvements are suggested.
Fair test
An investigation in which only one variable is changed while all other conditions are kept the same, so results can be reliably compared.
Hypothesis
A clear, testable statement predicting an outcome, which a practical food investigation is designed to support or reject through evidence.
Sensory evaluation
A structured method of judging food using the senses, often with tasting panels and rating or ranking tests to compare products objectively.
Star profile
A spider-diagram chart used in sensory analysis to plot scores for attributes such as taste, texture, colour and aroma of a food product.
